_comment: Curated Belize-specific seasonal highlights — matches Kakao Map's own seasonal-layer pattern (its cherry-blossom map), reused here for real Belize fishery/wildlife seasons. Hand-maintained, not live-computed: no API/feed exists for any of these. See docs/research/13-belize-seasonal-highlights-sourcing.md for full sourcing and why confidence differs per entry (lobster is one fixed official date range; queen conch is quota-driven and closes early most years; whale sharks and turtle nesting are real but don't reduce to one official date the way lobster does). activeWindow uses month/day (1-12 / 1-31); startMonth > endMonth means the window wraps across the new year (lobster's open season, not shown here since the *closed* season is what's flagged as the highlight, does not wrap: see each entry). Re-verify at least once a year and update lastVerifiedAt when touched.

highlights.name: Lobster season closed
highlights.description: Spiny lobster fishing is closed March 1 - June 30 nationwide to protect the breeding season, reopening July 1. This is the closed window, not the open one, since that's the more useful heads-up for a visitor expecting lobster on the menu.
highlights.confidence: High — official regulator page, consistently corroborated by current-year news each season.

highlights.name: Queen conch season closed (approximate)
highlights.description: Queen conch harvesting is nominally closed July 1 - September 30, but Belize closes it early every recent year once the national catch quota is met (as early as April in the 2025-26 season) — treat the true closure as "probably already in effect" for much of this window, not a hard boundary.
highlights.source: Belize Fisheries Department (fisheries.gov.bz/regulations); Belize Fisheries Department season-closure announcements (thereporter.bz, breakingbelizenews.com, sanpedrosun.com, 2026)
highlights.confidence: Medium — official nominal range, but quota-driven early closures mean the real closure date varies year to year and isn't predictable in advance.

highlights.name: Whale sharks at Gladden Spit

location.label: Gladden Spit and Silk Cayes Marine Reserve

highlights.description: Whale sharks gather at Gladden Spit, about 90 minutes by boat from Placencia, to feed on spawning Cubera snapper — most reliable for a few days around the full moons of April, May, and June. Book through a licensed Placencia dive operator.
highlights.source: Splash Dive Center (licensed Placencia dive operator); Heyman et al., Journal of Fish Biology (2005); Belize Fisheries Department (fisheries.gov.bz/gsscmr)
highlights.confidence: Medium — real and well-documented, but tourism-operator guidance and peer-reviewed science give slightly different day-counts around each full moon, so this is shown as a broad month window rather than an exact date.

highlights.name: Sea turtle nesting season
highlights.description: Hawksbill, loggerhead, and green turtles nest at sites including Gales Point/Manatee Bar, Half Moon Caye, and South Water Caye — peak activity is June-July. No single Belize authority publishes one national date range (this composites Belize Audubon Society's and SEA Belize's own site-specific windows), so treat this as a helpful approximation, not an official boundary.
highlights.source: Belize Audubon Society (Half Moon Caye); SEA Belize; ECOMAR
highlights.confidence: Medium — real nesting activity, well-documented at the site level, but composited from several site-specific managing bodies rather than one national source.

highlights.name: Gales Point / Manatee Bar (hawksbill nesting)
highlights.description: One of the most important hawksbill turtle nesting sites in the western Caribbean, an 8km stretch of beach near Gales Point village.
highlights.confidence: Medium — site and species well-documented; exact date range composited, see turtle-nesting-season entry.

highlights.name: Half Moon Caye (turtle nesting)

location.label: Half Moon Caye Natural Monument, Lighthouse Reef Atoll

highlights.description: Loggerhead, green, and hawksbill turtles all nest here — hatchlings emerge roughly 55-65 days later, peaking September-October.
highlights.confidence: High for this specific site — the managing body's own published window.

highlights.name: South Water Caye (hawksbill nesting)
highlights.description: A monitored hawksbill nesting hotspot within South Water Caye Marine Reserve.
highlights.source: Hawksbill Sea Turtle Recovery Program monitoring (secondary sourcing — see docs/research/13)
highlights.confidence: Medium — site and species documented via secondary sources rather than the monitoring program's own page directly.
